vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: fastfish-lite
Version: 1.0.4

The skill is classified as suspicious primarily due to its inherent supply chain risk. It explicitly instructs the OpenClaw agent to `git clone` and `pip install` dependencies from an external GitHub repository (https://github.com/superxs777/fastfish-lite.git) as part of its installation process, as detailed in `SKILL.md`. This creates a significant vulnerability where a compromise of the upstream repository could lead to arbitrary code execution on the host system. While `SKILL.md` includes strong prompt injection defenses for the agent (e.g., whitelisting `system.run` commands, forbidding credential exposure, restricting cron modifications), the fundamental reliance on untrusted external code for installation elevates the risk profile beyond benign.

llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed wrapper for installing and operating fastfish-lite, with expected but real supply-chain, credential, and scheduled-task risks.

dimensions.detail: Use of a local Python service, an external hot-topic API, and optional webhook/API credentials is proportionate to the feature set, with guidance to avoid root and use isolation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs users to clone a third-party GitHub repository, install Python requirements, and run its service; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but the reviewed artifact does not include or verify that external code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions constrain system.run to named scripts, require explicit user intent for installation, and prohibit exposing .env credentials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Scheduled crontab/OpenClaw Cron jobs are part of the daily push feature and are disclosed; the artifact also warns against editing, deleting, or updating cron jobs without explicit user direction.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented capabilities match the stated purpose: article formatting, local compliance checks, HTML preview, hot-topic retrieval, and optional messaging push.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the fastfish-lite repository and its dependencies. Use a virtual environment or container, avoid running as root, keep webhook/API keys narrowly scoped, and create scheduled push jobs only when you actually want persistent daily notifications.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The .env references are for documented API keys and messaging webhooks, and the artifact explicitly forbids displaying those secrets; this does not show credential theft in the skill text.
[YR1] expected: The cron references describe user-configured scheduled hot-topic pushes, not hidden persistence or a backdoor payload.
[T03] expected: External repository cloning and dependency installation are expected for this wrapper skill and are disclosed, but users should treat the external repo and dependencies as outside the reviewed artifact.
